reasons.A: Short, declarative sentences in many small paragraphs, a plain, briskly assertive tone and almost no hedging or semicolons; far from the author's long, qualified, reflective periods.
reasons.B: Right register and long clause-built sentences with semicolons and first-person hedges, but it piles on the qualifiers ('in some sense', 'arguably', 'precisely', 'rather', 'it seems to me', 'perhaps') more thickly than the passage does, so it reads as imitation.
reasons.C: Long, balanced sentences with measured first-person hedging ('I am less convinced', 'it seems to me', 'I think'), an occasional semicolon, a run of reflective questions and full paragraphs; closest to the author's movement and stance without overdoing it.
